questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement. 

Though many European t__raders visit Puducherry in the sixteenth century onwards__, what remains today is a relic of its French past.

options.text: trader visit Puducherry from the sixteenth century onwards
traders visited Puducherry in a sixteenth century onward
traders visited Puducherry from the sixteenth century onwards

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**traders visited Puducherry from the sixteenth century onwards**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, it is clear that the speaker is talking first about an event of the past that is being continued till date because the word **onwards** is used. So, the past form of the verb **visit **i.e. **visited** will be used.
 
• Also, **from** will be used in place of **in **because **from** is used to indicate initiation of an action which is the traders visiting Puducherry starting from the sixteenth century.
 
• 
 You can use 'from' when you are talking about the beginning of a period of time.

 **Examples:**

 
 
• *She studied painting from 1926 and also worked as a commercial artist.*
 
• *Breakfast is available to fishermen from 6 a.m.*
 
• *From 1922 till 1925 she lived in Prague.*
 
 
 
• 
 You can use** 'in'** to refer to something happens in a particular year, month, or other period of time, it happens during that time.

 **Example:**

 
 
• 
 Export orders improved in the last month.
 
 
 
 
• Also, from will be used in place of in because from is used to indicate initiation of an action which is the traders visiting Puducherry starting from the sixteenth century.

The correct sentence would be ''*Though many European **traders visited Puducherry from the sixteenth century onwards**, what remains today is a relic of its French past.''*

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. For a split second, as the stranger stepped into the light, his furry head was clearly visible.

B. At first, all seemed still outside the house,except for the sound of the rain.

C. Recognizing him, Joe stood petrified staring at the man wearing a long coat,wet from rain.

D. But then, footsteps approached the house and a stranger emerged out of the darkness.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

The first statement is **B **i.e. ***At first, all seemed still outside the house, except for the sound of the rain.* ** This is because the sentence begins with **at first **and out of all other statements, it clearly describes the starting of the situation described.

After **B,** it should be **D** ***But then, footsteps approached the house and a stranger emerged out of the darkness* **as it is in continuation with the first statement and describes the next event that takes place.

After **D,** it should be** A**, as the speaker gives a brief account of the stranger and then finally recognizes him in statement **C.**

**The order is BDAC.**

So, options** 2,3 and 4 **are** incorrect. **

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Most disputes can be solved amicably unless one are rigid.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

*Most disputes can be solved amicably **unless one are** rigid.*

The singular noun **one** does not agree with the plural verb **are**. Instead of **are**, it should be **is.** A singular noun requires a singular verb whereas a plural noun requires a plural verb for subject-verb agreement in a sentence.

The correct sentence is --***Most disputes can be solved amicably unless one is rigid.***

So, options** 1,3 and 4 **are** incorrect.**

questions.question:

The India consensus study__ highlight a benefits by addin__g domestic violence prevention approaches to current government policy
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

*The India consensus study** highlights the benefits of adding** domestic violence prevention approaches to current government policy.*

The subject should agree with the verb in the sentence. **The study** is a singular noun so it will take the singular form of the verb i.e **highlights.**

**A** is used when we are referring to a group in general but **the** is used when we are talking about a specific thing. So, **the** should come before **benefits. **Also, **of** should be used instead of **by **because the study highlights what the benefits **of** adding the approaches.

So, options** 1,2 and 4 **are** incorrect.**

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

She was seen sitting in the last row.

options.text: We have seen her sitting in the last row.
We saw her sitting in the last row.
We see her sitting in the last row.
We had seen her sitting in the last row.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

*We saw her sitting in the last row.*

The subject **she** will become the object while changing from passive to active voice. The given question contains **was seen sitting** which means that the active voice will be in the **past continuous tens**e. So, we change the past participle form of the verb **seen **to the **simple past tense** i.e **saw **.

So, options** 1,3 and 4 **are** incorrect.**

questions.question:

In the northern suburbs of Bengaluru, home to the bulk of the information technology industry, the water crisis is even worst.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

*In the northern suburbs of Bengaluru, home to the bulk of the information technology industry, the water crisis **is even worse***

The third degree of the adjective is used when a thing is surpassing all others in property or effect whereas the second degree is used when we do a comparison. In the given sentence, second degree of adjective should be used i.e **worse** instead of **worst **because it is preceded by the word **even** which means that the speaker is making a comparison with another place.

So, options** 2,3 and 4 **are** incorrect.**

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The enemy will have seized the fort before nightfall.

options.text: The fort will have been seized by the enemy before nightfall.
The fort would have been seized by the enemy before nightfall.
The enemy will seize the fort before nightfall
The enemy will be seized by the fort before nightfall

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

***The fort will have been seized by the enemy before nightfall.***

The given sentence is in future perfect tense identified by **will have**. Firstly, we interchange the subject and the object while converting it to the passive form. **The fort** will become the subject and the **enemy** will become an object in the passive voice. Also, **been** will be added according to the rules.

So, options **2,3 and 4 **are** incorrect.**
